AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  NOVEMBER 15, 2022
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF
ASSEMBLY BILL 361, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE
LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING:
YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE
ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED
THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT:
https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.

  6:00 PM
  REGULAR MEETING
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS

  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE
  Rick Ramirez, Mayor
  Ana Valencia, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.
   REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

INVOCATION
  Sudersan Nunna
  Rock of the Nations Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Hailey Ybanez
  Gonsalves Elementary

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to proclaim November as Native American Heritage month in the City of Norwalk.

  II.  City Council to proclaim November as Family Court Awareness Month in the City of Norwalk.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Presentation on PlanetBids.

  3.  Veteran’s Day Tribute video.

  4.  Senior Nutrition Program video.

  5.  Bi-Weekly Review.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES ON THE AGENDA - Staff recommends City Council
  waive reading in full of all ordinances on the agenda and declare that said titles which appear on the
  public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.

  2.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of
  November 1, 2022. 825-04

  Minutes

  3.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period October 16, 2022 –
  October 29, 2022, in the total amount of $1,029,232.65. 630

  Report

  4.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  October 25, 2022 through November 7, 2022 in the total amount of $3,117,453.08. 640

  Warrant Register
 5.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY - Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Oscar
  Gonzalez and the State of California, Department of Transportation. 830-07/19

  Report

6.  ASSEMBLY BILL 361 FINDINGS - Staff recommends City Council make the following findings:

  a.  City Council has reconsidered the circumstances of the state of emergency.

  b.  Both of the following circumstances exist (i) The state of emergency continues to directly impact
  the ability of the members to meet safely in person and (ii) City Council continues to impose or
  recommend measures to promote social distancing including remote or hybrid meeting
  participation. 825

  Report

7.  PURCHASE AGREEMENT – PURCHASE OF THREE PARATRANSIT VANS - Staff recommends City
  Council approve a Purchase Agreement with Creative Bus Sales, Inc. to acquire three Starcraft Allstar
  Class C paratransit vans in the amount of $385,125.48; and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  agreement and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget and it is within the City
  Manager’s signing authority, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report

8.  AWARD OF CONTRACT – ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT CONSULTING SERVICES - Staff
  recommends City Council award a contract to Kosmont Companies for economic development
  consulting services for the development of a three-year term in an amount not to exceed $125,000
  each year; and authorize the City Manager to execute an agreement and any amendments provided
  there is funding in the budget, and it is within the City Manager’s signing authority, on behalf of the City,
  in a form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report

9.  AUTHORIZATION TO SUBMIT ANNUAL SHORT RANGE TRANSIT PLAN FOR FISCAL YEARS 2023-
  2025 - Staff recommends City Council receive and file the Triennial Short Range Transit Plan, and
  authorize the Executive Director of Regional Transportation to submit the updated Short Range Transit
  Plan to Metro.

  Report

10. AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 2 - PUBLIC AFFAIRS AND COMMUNICATION SERVICES - Staff
  recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 2 to the agreement with Merino, Barajas &
  Associates, Inc. not to exceed $45,000 from November 1, 2022 to March 31, 2023; and authorize the
  City Manager to execute this amendment on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report

11. CORONAVIRUS PANDEMIC – NOVEMBER EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER UPDATE –
  Receive and file.

  Report

12. PROJECT NO. 7233 - AWARD OF CONTRACT FOR THE CONSTRUCTION OF THE INTELLIGENT
  TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM IMPROVEMENTS ON FIRESTONE BOULEVARD BETWEEN TARGET
  DRIVEWAY AND ROSECRANS AVENUE (FEDERAL PROJECT NO. HSIPL-5347(043)) – Staff
  recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 22-64, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK, AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2022/23 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE MEASURE R FUNDS FOR PROJECT NO. 7233 – INTELLIGENT
  TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM IMPROVEMENTS ALONG FIRESTONE BOULEVARD FROM
  TARGET DRIVEWAY TO ROSECRANS AVENUE, in the amount of $317,630; and
   b.  award a construction contract to Select Electric, Inc., in the amount of $1,310,500 for Project No.
  7233 Intelligent Transportation System improvements along Firestone Boulevard; and authorize
  the City Manager to execute the agreement with up to the 15% contingency if necessary, on behalf
  of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report

  13. PROJECT NOS. 7228, 7229, AND 7230 - RESOLUTION NO. 22-65 - BUDGET AMENDMENT – Staff
  recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 22-65, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2022/23 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE AVAILABLE PROPOSITION C FUNDS TO HIGHWAY SAFETY
  IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM CYCLE 6 – PROJECT NOS. 7228, 7229, & 7230, in the amount of
  $581,210; and

  b.  approve an amendment to the agreement with Select Electric, Inc. to expand the scope of work
  and continue to provide Construction Services for Traffic Signal Improvements on Rosecrans
  Avenue, Studebaker Road to Carmenita Road, City Project No. 7228 Federal-Aid Project No.
  HSIP-5347 (038) in the amount of $375,617.42; and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  amendment provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by
  the City Attorney; and

  c.  approve an amendment to the agreement with FCG Consultants, Inc. to expand the scope of work
  and continue to provide Construction Management Services for Traffic Signal Improvements on
  Rosecrans Avenue, Studebaker Road to Carmenita Road, City Project No. 7228 Federal-Aid
  Project No. HSIP-5347 (038) in the amount of $140,677.16; and authorize the City Manager to
  execute the amendment provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form
  approved by the City Attorney; and

  d.  approve an amendment to the agreement with International Line Builders, Inc. to expand the
  scope of work and continue to provide Construction Services for Traffic Signal Improvements
  along Studebaker Road from Rosecrans Avenue to Alondra Boulevard City Project No. 7229
  Federal-Aid Project No. HSIP-5347 (039) in the amount of $155,000; and authorize the City
  Manager to execute the amendment provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City,
  in a form approved by the City Attorney; and

  e.  approve an amendment to the agreement with GK & Associates to expand the scope of work and
  continue to provide Construction Management Services for Traffic Signal Improvements along
  Studebaker Road from Rosecrans Avenue to Alondra Boulevard City Project No. 7229 Federal-Aid
  Project No. HSIP-5347 (039) in the amount of $30,000; and authorize the City Manager to execute
  the amendment provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved
  by the City Attorney; and

  f.  approve an amendment to the agreement with KDC, Inc. dba Dynalectric to expand the scope of
  work and continue to provide Construction Services for Traffic Signal Improvements on San
  Antonio Drive-Norwalk Boulevard between Rosecrans Avenue and Civic Center Drive, and on
  Civic Center Drive between Norwalk Boulevard and Bloomfield Avenue, City Project No. 7230
  Federal-Aid Project No. HSIP-5347 (040) in the amount of $66,411.13; and authorize the City
  Manager to execute the amendment provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City,
  in a form approved by the City Attorney; and

  g.  approve an amendment to the agreement with FCG Consultants, Inc. to expand the scope of work
  and continue to provide Construction Management Services for Traffic Signal Improvements on
  San Antonio Drive-Norwalk Boulevard between Rosecrans Avenue and Civic Center Drive, and on
  Civic Center Drive between Norwalk Boulevard and Bloomfield Avenue, City Project No. 7230
  Federal-Aid Project No. HSIP-5347 (040) in the amount of $144,792.26; and authorize the City
  Manager to execute the amendment provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City,
  in a form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report

APPOINTMENTS
   14. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

PUBLIC HEARING

  15. ORDINANCE NO. 22-1738 – ADOPTING BY REFERENCE THE 2022 CALIFORNIA BUILDING,
  RESIDENTIAL, FIRE, PLUMBING, ELECTRICAL, MECHANICAL, EXISTING BUILDING, AND
  GREEN BUILDING STANDARDS CODES AND AMENDMENTS AND AMENDING THE NORWALK
  MUNICIPAL CODE - RESOLUTION NO. 22-63 – MODIFYING THE CALIFORNIA STANDARD CODES
  DUE TO LOCAL CLIMATIC, GEOLOGICAL OR TOPOGRAPHICAL CONDITIONS – Staff recommends
  City Council:

  a.  adopt Ordinance No. 22-1738, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK ADOPTING BY
  REFERENCE THE 2022 EDITIONS OF THE CALIFORNIA BUILDING, RESIDENTIAL, FIRE,
  PLUMBING, ELECTRICAL, MECHANICAL, EXISTING BUILDING, AND GREEN BUILDING
  STANDARDS CODES AND RELATED MODEL CODES, WITH APPENDICES AND
  AMENDMENTS THERETO; AND AMENDING THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE, and waive
  further reading;

  b.  adopt Resolution No. 22-63, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK MAKING EXPRESS FINDINGS AND DETERMINATIONS THAT MODIFICATIONS TO
  THE CALIFORNIA BUILDING, RESIDENTIAL, FIRE, PLUMBING, ELECTRICAL, MECHANICAL,
  EXISTING BUILDING, AND GREEN BUILDING STANDARDS CODES IN ORDINANCE NO. 22-
  1738 ARE REASONABLY NECESSARY BECAUSE OF LOCAL CLIMATIC, GEOLOGICAL OR
  TOPOGRAPHICAL CONDITIONS.

  Report

REPORTS

  16. PROJECT NO. 7357 - AWARD OF CONTRACT FOR FORMER TANK FARM – PARK EXPANSION -
  Staff recommends City Council approve an agreement with Griffin Structures for project management
  services for the development of the 15-acre Tank Farm to expand Holifield Park for a minimum three-
  year term in the amount of $856,500; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and
  any necessary amendments not to exceed a total agreement amount of $942,150, provided there is
  funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report

  17. CITY COUNCIL DISCUSSION AND DIRECTION ON DECLARING A HOMELESS STATE OF
  EMERGENCY – Provide direction to staff.

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated November 9, 2022.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
